parameters.query: =SELECT json_object_agg(e->>'key', core.fn_config_get(e->>'pkg', 'model', e->>'key')) AS model FROM jsonb_array_elements(($1::jsonb)->'items') AS e

=WITH adv AS (
  SELECT a.domain, a.plan_context, COALESCE(cs.scope, 'household') AS scope
  FROM core.advisors a
  LEFT JOIN core.context_scopes cs ON cs.context_name = a.plan_context
  WHERE NOT a.own_review_cron
),
pids AS (
  SELECT a.domain, p.person_id,
         (SELECT split_part(ap.full_name, ' ', 1) FROM agent.persons ap WHERE ap.person_id = p.person_id) AS person_name
  FROM adv a
  CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT person_id FROM agent.fn_context_persons(a.plan_context) WHERE a.scope = 'per_user'
    UNION ALL
    SELECT NULL::text WHERE a.scope <> 'per_user'
  ) p
),
ev AS MATERIALIZED (
  SELECT person_name, core.fn_advisor_review_evaluate(domain, person_id, '{}'::jsonb) AS r FROM pids
),
agg AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(al || jsonb_build_object('person_name', ev.person_name)), '[]'::jsonb) AS alerts
  FROM ev CROSS JOIN LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(ev.r->'alerts') al
)
SELECT agg.alerts::text AS alerts,
       core.fn_ui_texts_for(jsonb_build_object('keys', to_jsonb(ARRAY['core.advisor.drift_title','core.advisor.drift_cta','core.advisor.footer_off','core.advisor.btn_off','core.fmt.empty','core.fmt.default_suffix','core.fmt.yes','core.fmt.no','core.fmt.removed']::text[]), 'doc', agg.alerts))::text AS ui
FROM agg;

parameters.text: ={{ 'Rewrite the following periodic advisor check-in as a short, friendly Telegram message, written in the language ' + $json.language_label + '. PLAIN TEXT only (no markdown, no asterisks). Keep EVERY number, amount and date EXACTLY as written (do not reformat them) and keep every warning or hint sentence. Maximum 16 lines. Text:\n\n' + $json.det_text }}

parameters.content:
## DB-Automatik
**Generische Core-Advisor-Engine (Latch entscheidet DB, LLM nur Phrasing)**

Täglicher Drift-Wächter (schedule.drift_check 10:00, aus core.config, änderbar per lifeagents config set). Iteriert core.advisors, rechnet Soll-Ist-Drift + Staleness, LATCHT (geteilte core.notification_state, source=advisor:domain): nur eine NEU gebreachte Metrik schickt -> stiller Lauf = keine Message (kein Tages-Spam), Re-Arm wenn wieder im Band. F9-Gate (Cron on?): core.fn_package_active(core) AND core.fn_config_get(core,cron_enable,drift_check)=true (DB entscheidet, fail-closed; default false = opt-in bis ein Plan publiziert ist). Läuft 10:00 VOR cron_review (10:05) -> Breaches zuerst hier gefangen + gelatcht. Build message rendert die paket-gelieferte alert.msg-Struktur in Owner-Sprache (geteilter Renderer, Zahlen per Intl; Texte aus derselben Anweisung wie der Latch); Phrase formuliert in dieser Sprache um (model.advisor_review, jede Zahl wörtlich), onError continue -> deterministischer Fallback. WS-3 Phase A: der Send trägt einen Abschalten-Inline-Button (callback_data cron_off:drift_check) -> der Owner schaltet diesen Wächter-Cron per Tipp ab (Orchestrator-Callback -> core.fn_set_cron_enable, core.config cron_enable); Re-Aktivieren per /reminders (Roter Faden Paket B).

## DB-Automatik
**core.fn_advisor_review_evaluate (Registry-Dispatch + Latch, off-canvas)**

Evaluate advisors FÄCHERT core.advisors x Personen (P2b-2 Get-AdvisorFanoutCte: per_user-Domains wie career je Person via agent.fn_context_persons(plan_context), household-Domains wie finance mit person_id=NULL) und ruft je (Domain, Person) core.fn_advisor_review_evaluate(domain, person_id) (MATERIALIZED CTE -> die VOLATILE Eval-fn läuft EXAKT 1x je (Advisor, Person)). Der Core-Wrapper: Registry-Lookup domain->review_fn (z. B. finance.fn_advisor_review), dyn. EXECUTE, dann LATCH gegen die geteilte core.notification_state (source=advisor:domain[:person_id]) über core.fn_should_notify/fn_notify_reconcile (Erst-/Re-Breach -> send=true; bereits fired -> still; wieder im Band -> Re-Arm via Reconcile-GC räumt stale metric_keys; person_id=NULL byte-gleich heute). Läuft unter dem Haupt-RW-Credential (Build-Pg-Default) — die fn SCHREIBT Latch-State (Präzedenz cron_monitor_check_triggers). GENERIK: der Cron kennt keine Paket-Felder, er rendert die paket-gelieferte Struktur (alert.msg / digest.lines) in Owner-Sprache, die Texte kommen aus derselben Anweisung wie der Latch (core.fn_ui_texts_for); model.advisor_review formuliert in dieser Sprache um (jede Zahl wörtlich) (Load model config liest es bei JEDEM Lauf VOR Evaluate -> ein Ladefehler stoppt den Lauf, bevor ein Latch geschrieben ist; Umschalter mit einem Knoten je Claude-Modell), onError continue -> Fallback = der deterministische Text (Choose text). Build message setzt report=false -> Quiet run (keine Message).
